songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dark Star and soaring The Eleven; marathon Lovelight despite muddy tape
ai_show_review.blurb: Features a powerful Dark Star and an extended Turn On Your Lovelight that closes the second set. China Cat Sunflower > High Time flows into a tight jam, while The Eleven showcases intricate rhythmic interplay. Soundboard capture is fair with noticeable mud and hiss.
ai_show_review.review: The July 5, 1969 Electric Theater show captures the Dead at a wild, high‑energy peak of their late‑60s era. Jerry’s guitar roars through an expansive Dark Star that feels both raw and inspired, even if a few phrases wobble in Saint Stephen and The Eleven. Pigpen’s organ and vocal swagger drive Hard To Handle and Turn On Your Lovelight, the latter stretching into a marathon closing that highlights the band’s improvisational stamina. China Cat Sunflower segues smoothly into High Time, delivering a bright, cohesive second‑set opener before the group dives into the tight, rhythmic gymnastics of The Eleven. While the soundboard tape suffers from muddy mids and persistent hiss—especially on “It’s All Over Now Baby Blue”—the performance itself is compelling enough that listeners will forgive the technical flaws to hear one of the era’s most exhilarating jams.

best_recording.reason: Only available soundboard; despite mud and hiss it captures the full set with decent stereo separation, making it the definitive source for this show.

key_highlights: Expansive Dark Star with raw guitar intensity
Marathon Turn On Your Lovelight closing showcases improvisational stamina
Tight interplay on The Eleven and seamless China Cat Sunflower > High Time transition
Fair soundboard recording that preserves the high‑energy vibe despite tape mud

band_performance.Jerry: Raw power on Dark Star; occasional phrasing slips in Saint Stephen and The Eleven, but overall leads the band with inspired solos.
band_performance.Mickey: Provides solid rhythmic drive throughout the set.
band_performance.Billy: Keeps a steady pulse supporting the improvisations.
